newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government calls 23rd confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy government calls 23rd confidence vote.

text.p: The Italian government on Tuesday called a confidence vote in the lower house on a decree law aimed at speeding up the approval process for starting or resuming state construction programmes.

The move, announced by Public Works Minister Paolo Costa, was to sweep away some 400 amendments tabled by the separatist Northern League. The vote will be the 23rd faced by the centre-left government since taking office last year.
The vote cannot be held until 24 hours have elapsed from it being formally called in parliament.
The government was forced to call the confidence vote to prevent the decree law from expiring.

Under a constitutional court ruling, decree laws passed by the cabinet have a 60 day life and must be either passed by parliament within that time or lapse. The construction decree law must be passed by May 25.

The decree law would create special authorities to streamline the approval process for starting or resuming public works that have been long frozen or stalled. The upper house has already approved the measure.
